title: Gardenio — Fleet Capacity & Placement
description: The placement-side companion to control-plane-liveness (feature ka-0000000905, GRADE 2026-08-19). Answers one operator question — can the fleet actually PLACE the agents it wants to run right now, and is the thing that places them alive? Pod-phase flow (Pending->Running->Succeeded) surfaces a stuck-Pending backlog before it is a capacity incident; the pending-pod gauge is the saturation headline; node-lifecycle churn shows Karpenter turning nodes over underneath; the reconcile dead-man is the second, independent liveness of the controller that drives placement; and the compaction leaderboard shows which agents are burning turns (and therefore holding capacity) on context compaction. Every panel is grounded in a metric with live series verified against gardenio-vmsingle this iteration.

options.content: **Fleet capacity & placement** — can the fleet place the agents it wants to run, and is the placer alive? **#6 Pending-pod saturation**: `gardenio_agent_pods_pending` climbing = we are running out of node capacity to place agent pods. **#4 Pod-phase flow**: `gardenio_agent_pod_phase_transitions_total` — watch `Pending->Running` keep pace with spawns; a stuck-`Pending` backlog is a capacity incident forming. **#9 Node churn**: `gardenio_node_lifecycle_events_total{reason}` — Karpenter deleting/disrupting/terminating nodes underneath the fleet. **#5 Reconcile dead-man**: `gardenio_reconcile_total` — the reconciler that drives placement MUST tick ~1/min; a flatlined counter means placement has silently stopped (second independent liveness, advice ka-0000005924). **#1 Compaction pressure**: `gardenio_agent_compactions_current` — which agents are burning turns on context compaction and holding capacity.

panels.title: #6 Agent pods Pending now (placement saturation)
panels.description: sum(gardenio_agent_pods_pending): total agent pods currently stuck in the Pending phase across all (project, role) — i.e. desired but not yet placed onto a node. This is the headline capacity-saturation number: a non-zero value that persists means Karpenter/the scheduler cannot find room and new agents are queueing behind node provisioning. Amber >0 (something is waiting), red at 5 (a real placement backlog). Pairs with the deferred-wait SLO.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_agent_pods_pending series. Empty is AMBIGUOUS here and this panel cannot resolve it: the reconciler Reset()s the gauge every sweep and re-Sets only (project, role) keys that actually have Pending pods, so an idle-healthy fleet and a dark reconciler render the same nothing. Resolve with the independent target “#5 Reconcile dead-man — reconciles/min” to the right — if that is ticking, this really is zero pods pending.

panels.title: #5 Reconcile dead-man — reconciles/min
panels.description: sum(rate(gardenio_reconcile_total[10m])) * 60: the agent controller's reconcile loop rate, per minute. The reconciler is what turns desired agents into placed pods, so this is a direct liveness signal for placement itself — steady-state is ~1 reconcile/min (the controller's resync cadence). A value at or near ZERO while agents are still desired means the placer has silently stopped: pods will sit un-created with no error anywhere (the second, independent control-plane liveness measure, advice ka-0000005924). Thresholds INVERT the usual sense — red at 0 (dead), amber below 0.1/min, green once it is ticking.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_reconcile_total series — the reconcile loop has not incremented since this controller booted, or the controller is not being scraped. Empty is strictly worse than a 0/min reading: the dead-man itself is blind. Check up{component="agents"} on Gardenio — System Health.

panels.title: #6 Pending agent pods by project × role
panels.description: sum by (project, role) (gardenio_agent_pods_pending): the pending-pod saturation broken out by (project, role) so a placement backlog can be attributed — e.g. a single greedy project's crew pods soaking up all the newly-provisioned capacity, or a role whose resource request no nodepool can satisfy. A band that stays lit for minutes (rather than a brief spike while a node spins up) is the signature of a genuine capacity shortfall for that slice.

defaults.noValue: no (project, role) row rendered. The panel filters gardenio_agent_pods_pending > 0 and the reconciler Reset()s that gauge every sweep, so empty is AMBIGUOUS and this panel cannot resolve it: either nothing is pending, or nothing was swept. Resolve with the independent target “#5 Reconcile dead-man — reconciles/min” — if it is ticking, this really is zero pending pods.

panels.title: #4 Pod-phase flow — transitions/min into each phase
panels.description: sum by (phase_to) (rate(gardenio_agent_pod_phase_transitions_total[$__rate_interval])) * 60: the rate at which agent pods are ENTERING each lifecycle phase. Pending = new spawns landing; Running = successful placements; Succeeded = clean completions. In a healthy fleet the Running line tracks the Pending line with only a short placement lag; a Pending line that outruns Running for a sustained window is the leading indicator of a stuck-Pending backlog — a capacity incident forming — before the pending-pod gauge above even saturates.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_agent_pod_phase_transitions_total series — no agent pod has changed phase since this controller booted, so the counter does not exist. On an idle fleet this is legitimate; on a busy one it means the controller is dark (check the dead-man above).

panels.title: #4 Pod-phase transition matrix (this range)
panels.description: sum by (phase_from, phase_to) (increase(gardenio_agent_pod_phase_transitions_total[$__range])): the full from->to transition count over the selected window, so the SHAPE of the flow is legible at a glance. Pending->Running dominating is healthy churn. A material Running->Pending count is pods being evicted/rescheduled (node churn or preemption — cross-check #9). Rows are sorted by count so the dominant transition is on top.

defaults.noValue: no pod-phase transitions in the selected range — no agent pod started or stopped in the window. Widen the range; the matrix is a $__range increase(), so a short window on a quiet fleet is legitimately empty.

panels.title: #9 Node lifecycle churn by reason
panels.description: sum by (reason) (rate(gardenio_node_lifecycle_events_total[$__rate_interval])) * 60: how fast agent nodes are turning over, split by reason (deleting / disrupting / not_ready / terminated). This is Karpenter and the kubelet moving the ground underneath the fleet — a burst here that lines up with Running->Pending in the transition matrix (#4) or a spike in the pending gauge (#6) is node churn evicting running agents and forcing re-placement. Correlate with involuntary-deaths to see whether churn is costing agent lives.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_node_lifecycle_events_total series — no agent node was created, disrupted or deleted since this controller booted. Stable capacity is the healthy reading; corroborate with the reconcile dead-man before calling it stable.

panels.title: #5 Reconcile rate by result (second liveness measure)
panels.description: sum by (result) (rate(gardenio_reconcile_total[$__rate_interval])) * 60: the reconcile loop rate over time, split by result (ok / error). This is the timeseries counterpart to the reconcile dead-man stat — it plots the loop actually ticking and surfaces a rising error result before the overall rate flatlines. A line that drops to and stays at zero while agents are still desired is the unambiguous 'placer wedged' signature (advice ka-0000005924: measure the same liveness two independent ways).

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_reconcile_total series — the same absence the dead-man stat reports, seen over time. A live reconciler always draws a result="ok" line; empty means the controller is not being scraped, not that reconciles are failing.

panels.title: #1 Compaction pressure leaderboard (agents compacting now)
panels.description: topk(15, gardenio_agent_compactions_current): the agents currently mid-compaction, ranked. Compaction is a direct token-cost and latency tax — an agent compacting is burning turns re-summarising its own context instead of doing work, and it holds its pod (and therefore capacity) for longer while it does. No other board surfaces this PER-AGENT; cost-overview and context-observability only show the fleet-wide aggregate. A recurring offender here is a candidate for a tighter prompt or a smaller advice footprint (advice-hygiene). Sorted by compaction count, hottest agent on top.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_agent_compactions_current series. This is NOT “no agent is compacting”: the controller publishes one series per agent in its sweep — value 0 for an agent that has never compacted — so a live controller over a live fleet always renders rows. Empty means no agents were swept at all, or the controller is dark. Corroborate with “#5 Reconcile dead-man — reconciles/min” below.

panels.title: #6 Pending-pod pressure distribution over the window — p50 / p95 / p99 / max

defaults.noValue: the pending gauge is not reporting — placement pressure is UNKNOWN, not zero

panels.description: The Pending stat at the top is an instant: it reads 0 the moment a backlog drains, so chronic saturation and a momentary blip look identical. These quantiles are taken over the whole dashboard range, so a p50 above zero means the fleet is CONSTANTLY waiting on placement, while p50 at zero with a high max is one spike worth ignoring.

panels.title: #6 Pending agent pods by role (now)

defaults.noValue: nothing Pending right now, or the pending gauge is not reporting — the reconcile dead-man stat at the top of the board says which

panels.description: Which workload class is waiting for a node right now, ranked. The timeseries above splits by project × role over time; this is the one-glance 'who is stuck' read that goes with the Pending stat at the top.
